Source: A 27-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for an abnormal vaginal discharge.
She has a medical history of asthma, IV drug abuse, and depression.
The patient has engaged in unprotected intercourse with 12 different partners.
The patient is given antibiotics and is advised on safe sex practices.
She has 1 to 2 alcoholic drinks per day.
She states that every time she has sex a rash has emerged on her skin.
Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 127/68 mmHg, pulse is 91/min, respirations are 14/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.
She feels ashamed of her behavior and is requesting treatment for her condition and advice for safe sex.
The patient presents to the emergency department 3 days later with a complaint of a rash.
